summary: Yes, the model is well-calibrated: a gradient-boosted classifier trained on the Adult Income data has an Expected Calibration Error of 0.008 (0.8 percentage points) across 10 probability bins on held-out test data, and predicted probabilities track observed >50K rates closely across the full range. A logistic regression baseline is similarly well-calibrated (ECE=0.0083), and post-hoc isotonic recalibration did not improve (slightly worsened) the gradient boosting model's calibration, confirming it was not meaningfully miscalibrated to begin with.
primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (10-bin, Gradient Boosting, test set)
direction: model is well-calibrated (ECE ≈ 0.008, low across all probability bins)
methodological_choices: Target defined as class=='>50K' (76%/24% class imbalance, left as-is/no resampling since calibration assessment benefits from natural base rates). 75/25 stratified train/test split (random_state=42). Numeric features standardized, categorical features one-hot encoded (unknown categories ignored), '?' values kept as their own category rather than imputed. Two models compared: LogisticRegression (max_iter=2000) as a baseline expected to be well-calibrated by construction, and GradientBoostingClassifier (300 trees, depth 3, lr=0.1) as the primary/best-performing model (higher AUC=0.928, lower Brier=0.088). Calibration measured via equal-width (10-bin) reliability diagrams, Expected Calibration Error (sample-weighted mean |observed freq - mean predicted prob| per bin), Maximum Calibration Error (worst-bin gap), and Brier score, all computed on the same held-out test set used for AUC. As a robustness check, additionally fit isotonic recalibration (via CalibratedClassifierCV/FrozenEstimator on a 70/30 split of the training data) on top of the gradient boosting model and re-evaluated on the same test set; recalibration did not improve ECE/MCE/Brier, supporting the conclusion that the base model's probabilities were already reasonably calibrated rather than the improvement being masked by a mis-specified recalibration step. An alternative choice would have been quantile (equal-frequency) binning instead of equal-width, which can give different ECE estimates especially given the skewed distribution of predicted probabilities (most mass near 0).
